description: Append-oriented empirical history of HumanityAI operational system-design experiments and changes. This file records observed outcomes and interpretations but grants no authority and cannot override protected governance, security, licensing, constitutional, scheduler, or permission boundaries.

records.problem_trigger: Recent adaptive slots produced substantial repository activity but comparatively low decision progress, with overlapping allocation and verification responsibilities and repeated baseline/brief/candidate-verification cycles.
records.prior_design: Peer-like adaptive workers independently selected high-value safe work, with multiple workers able to research, verify, synthesize, and redirect priorities. Independent Audit existed, but ordinary management/integration ownership was diffuse.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Separating ordinary management from first-line production, second-line verification, and third-line assurance should reduce duplicated compute, increase decision delta per slot, preserve verifier independence, and make integration responsibility explicit without expanding authority.
records.exact_change: Transitioned ordinary operations toward Human/constitution -> Controller D -> Operators A/B -> independent Verifier C -> independent Audit. D owns portfolio allocation, routine internal integration, design memory, and GitLab mirror maintenance. A biases toward direct progress; B preserves exploration; C independently challenges Tier-2 A/B work; Audit remains independent assurance. Introduced risk-tiered integration and a durable portfolio state in agent/portfolio.json.
records.decision_delta_metric: A slot is high-yield when it changes a belief, decision, capability, ranking, uncertainty estimate, adoption judgment, measurable outcome model, or future compute allocation. Repository growth and commit count are not success metrics.

risk_tiered_integration.tier_1: Routine reversible unprotected housekeeping/tooling; exact-head CI required; C optional; D integrates.
risk_tiered_integration.tier_2: Substantive A/B evidence, prioritization, registry, analytical/code, or decision products; exact-head CI plus independent C verdict required before D integration.
risk_tiered_integration.tier_3: Protected/security/governance/licensing/constitutional/agent-authority changes, external PRs, unresolved injection/provenance compromise, or consequential external action; human review required.

expected_benefit: Higher decision delta per unit of scheduled compute.
Less duplicate baseline and verification work.
Clear ordinary integration ownership without weakening human gates.
Stronger independence between production, verification, and assurance.
Durable allocation state that reduces dependence on conversational memory.
risks: D could become an allocation bottleneck or create excessive centralization within the ordinary operational layer.
A/B exploration could narrow too aggressively if portfolio guidance overfits recent evidence.
C verification latency could reduce throughput for Tier-2 work.
Decision-delta language could Goodhart toward visible reallocation rather than genuine usefulness.
Control-plane artifacts could become stale or bureaucratic if updated without material changes.
records.evaluation_window: Initial 6-24 hours, then periodic review after enough A/B/C integration cycles exist.
evaluation_criteria: Share of recent slots producing material decision delta rather than generic artifacts.
Duplicate-work rate and repeated low-stakes verification rate.
Number of Tier-2 producer claims materially corrected or blocked by independent C review.
Time from useful A/B proposal to safe D integration.
Whether portfolio updates redirect multiple future slots rather than merely document activity.
Whether Audit identifies loss of independence, control bottlenecks, unsafe integration, or Goodhart behavior.

observed_outcomes.observation: Operator A produced PR #80 as a decision-oriented compute-allocation product rather than another baseline, proposing UCT cost/adoption modeling and an ALMP evidence refresh. It remained unmerged pending C review as required.
Operator B produced PR #81 exploring a newer youth-ALMP synthesis and made explicit START/MORE/LESS/STOP recommendations capable of redirecting multiple P07 slots.

Independent C returned C-VERDICT: QUALIFY on PR #81. C preserved the useful allocation signal but identified overstatement about modality reversal, publication-bias handling, and comparability. D did not integrate the uncorrected Tier-2 work.

failures_side_effects: No completed Tier-2 D integration cycle had yet demonstrated end-to-end producer -> independent verifier -> controller merge throughput at this checkpoint.
PR #80 remained awaiting C verdict, so verifier capacity/latency was still an open operational variable.
The design had not yet been observed long enough to establish that higher early decision orientation persisted rather than reflecting novelty.
lessons: Independent qualification is already adding value by preserving a useful reallocation while blocking a stronger unsupported causal/effect interpretation.
The controller should consume C adverse verdicts as allocation signals rather than override them.
Portfolio updates should encode corrected uncertainty and stop conditions, not merely restate producer recommendations.
Do not declare the hierarchy proven until several end-to-end cycles and independent Audit observations exist.

records.problem_trigger: The new hierarchy needed evidence that independent verification could both change producer claims and still permit useful work to reach main without D overriding C or becoming a permanent bottleneck.
records.prior_design: DH0001 had shown one C QUALIFY block but no completed Tier-2 producer -> C -> D integration cycle.
records.hypothesis_rationale: If the separation-of-duties design is functioning, C should be able to independently PASS a decision-bearing product after reproducing its key claims, and D should then integrate only the exact reviewed head after successful CI.
records.exact_change: No architecture authority changed. Operator B produced PR #84 under the existing portfolio; C independently returned PASS at exact head 6b39ab902b412487b9e5b7ed6ecb2ca014116ba2; D confirmed the single unprotected research-file scope, exact-head successful Validate HumanityAI run 34167160907, and no unresolved review threads, then squash-merged through the normal PR path as main 113452710749499439b6365204cf1b27d756ced2. Portfolio allocation was then narrowed toward study-level LMIC ALMP cost/adoption extraction.
expected_benefit: Demonstrate end-to-end Tier-2 throughput without weakening C independence.
Convert verified cost/adoption evidence into a sharper next exploration target.
Reduce repeated global ALMP meta-summary work.
risks: One successful integration cycle is too little evidence to declare the hierarchy proven.
C review latency remains measurable because PR #80 still awaits verdict.
D could overreact to a single ALMP result and overconcentrate the portfolio on P07.
records.evaluation_window: Continue through several additional A/B/C cycles and at least one independent Audit review.
evaluation_criteria: Whether subsequent Tier-2 work continues to receive independent challenge before integration.
Whether C PASS/QUALIFY/FAIL outcomes materially affect D allocation and merge decisions.
Whether time-to-integration remains acceptable without bypassing review.
Whether portfolio diversity is preserved while low-yield repetition declines.

observed_outcomes.observation: C reproduced PR #84's decision-bearing cost medians from the primary ILO/World Bank brief and explicitly preserved the non-portability and selected cost-effectiveness caveats.
D integrated PR #84 only after exact-head CI success and C PASS, completing the first observed end-to-end Tier-2 integration cycle under DH0001.

The early hierarchy is producing material decision delta: B's next allocation moved from broad modality synthesis to a study-level cost/adoption question with explicit insufficient-comparability kill tests.

failures_side_effects: PR #80 still lacks a C verdict, so verifier queue latency has not been resolved.
PR #81 remains qualified and partly superseded by the verified allocation signal in PR #84; integrating it now may have low marginal value unless narrowed.
lessons: Exact-head independent verification can coexist with useful throughput when producer scope is narrow and decision-bearing claims are reproducible.
A qualified earlier artifact need not be forced through correction when a later independently verified artifact captures the useful decision delta more cleanly.
Continue measuring decision delta and verifier latency; do not optimize for number of integration cycles.

records.problem_trigger: Audit finding #111 and subsequent controller runs exposed stale controller assignments, duplicate/superseded producer work, branch-freshness rework, verifier/integrator queue aging, and repeated bookkeeping that could consume capacity without increasing decision progress.
records.prior_design: D used a durable portfolio and risk-tiered integration, but there was no mandatory post-integration coherence gate, no explicit hard Tier-2 WIP limit, incomplete delegation contracts, and no process-error/toil threshold requiring simplification.
records.hypothesis_rationale: Finish-before-start flow control, a hard default WIP limit of two Tier-2 candidates, mandatory post-integration reconciliation, explicit assignment contracts, and aging/toil/error-budget triggers should reduce stale or duplicate execution and shorten useful producer-to-verifier-to-integration flow without weakening C or Audit independence.
records.exact_change: Within existing ordinary-management authority, D adopted the human-approved 2026-09-09 controller-coherence gate and Audit #111 flow standard: reconcile portfolio against canonical main and live PR state before new Tier-2 allocation; hold production while stale; perform post-integration coherence checks; cap active Tier-2 C/D WIP at two absent a documented higher-EV exception; require each A/B Tier-2 assignment to state decision question, why now, expected delta, scope, output, kill condition, and downstream decision; act on unexplained aging beyond two healthy D cycles; and simplify/hold when recovery toil or repeated process errors dominate. Scheduler cadence, permissions, constitutional authority, C independence, and Audit authority were unchanged.
expected_benefit: Less verifier and integrator queue aging.
Higher fraction of compute finishing decision-bearing work before starting more.
Controller state that reflects live canonical reality rather than conversational residue.
risks: A hard WIP cap can underutilize compute when C/D capacity is temporarily idle.
Frequent coherence bookkeeping can itself become toil or stale branches.
Holding production may overcorrect after transient queue congestion.
Assignment-contract detail can become bureaucracy if it does not change execution.
records.evaluation_window: Next 6-12 healthy controller cycles, with an earlier checkpoint if duplicate/stale failures recur or recovery/toil approaches half of capacity across three controller windows.
evaluation_criteria: Count of active Tier-2 candidates stays at or below two absent documented exception.
Merged/closed/superseded work is removed before replacement allocation.
Producer-ready to C-verdict to integration/closure aging does not remain unexplained beyond two healthy D cycles.
Duplicate or stale producer PRs decline relative to the preceding controller windows.
Recovery/bookkeeping does not dominate roughly half of operational capacity across three controller windows.
Independent C adverse verdicts continue to block or narrow Tier-2 integration rather than being bypassed.

observed_outcomes.observation: Controller reconciliation closed or deprioritized superseded work and repeatedly held replacement Tier-2 production while verification/integration queues were congested.

PR #94 was ultimately integrated after exact-head CI and independent C PASS, and the post-integration controller state removed it from active WIP; current active Tier-2 WIP is zero while deferred PRs #95 and #70 are explicitly outside WIP.

At the 2026-09-10 checkpoint, canonical portfolio still held new Tier-2 production because this design-history checkpoint was overdue, demonstrating that the coherence gate can stop obsolete or premature replacement allocation.
The remediation appears to have improved finish-before-start discipline, but the amount of reconciliation/freshness work remains a material cost and the design is not yet proven.

failures_side_effects: Several controller windows were consumed by stale-state reconciliation, branch freshness, duplicate/superseded PR cleanup, or mirror recovery rather than direct mission analysis.
The mandatory checkpoint itself became overdue long enough to hold otherwise available producer capacity.
GitLab mirror provenance is currently stale/incomplete relative to canonical GitHub and requires separate recovery; this checkpoint does not claim mirror health.
lessons: Finish-before-start and live-state reconciliation should remain, but controller bookkeeping must be kept small and tied to actual allocation changes.
Refresh producer branches before final C review when practical, and avoid nonessential main mutations between fresh PASS and integration.
Deferred work is not active WIP and should not consume C capacity without a concrete downstream decision.
A mandatory control checkpoint should be recorded promptly so the safeguard does not itself create prolonged idle capacity.
Do not release new Tier-2 production until this checkpoint is canonical and a fresh coherence check confirms live state.
